title: Rate limit policy matrix (tier x route) — hot-route capacity protection (WIP)
content:
Last updated: 2026-01-22 (post us-east canary + first round of EU tuning)
Owner: Cole Summers (Quotas)
Primary readers: API Gateway, Routing, SRE, Product (Hosted API)

Purpose
- Draft policy matrix for tier-aware rate limiting + quotas per hot route.
- Intended as the single “defaults” reference for policy config migration (route_groups + tier defaults).
- WIP: numbers are starting points; we expect tuning per region based on scheduler lag + queue depth signals.

Definitions / glossary
- “Rate limit”: short-window token-bucket at gateway (request-based). Enforced with 429 + Retry-After.
- “Burst”: max instantaneous bucket size for short spikes (token-bucket capacity).
- “Quota”: longer-window budget (requests/day and/or tokens/day). Evaluated in quota service; 429 with quota reason.
- “Protected route”: route group that participates in admission control and priority budgets (enterprise preserved; best-effort shed earlier).
- “Enterprise priority”: contract/SLA traffic on shared Hosted fleet (and some Dedicated control planes), eligible for priority routing.
- “Best-effort”: any non-enterprise tier under pressure; should be throttled/shedded first to protect fleet.

Reason codes (target state; see docs PR)
- 429 reason=quota_exceeded (quota service)
- 429 reason=tier_rate_limit (gateway bucket)
- 429 reason=overload_shed (routing/admission control under pressure)
- 503 reason=capacity_unavailable (rare; only when we cannot safely apply controlled shedding; should trend to ~0)

Assumptions / constraints
- Keep data plane overhead low: policy evaluation uses (route_group, tier, region) + optional “customer override id” (allowlist only).
- Avoid high cardinality: do NOT encode per-model or per-tenant metrics into policy tags.
- Separate “route groups” from literal routes to keep config stable across API versions.

Route groups (current)
- chat: /v1/chat/completions
- embeddings: /v1/embeddings
- rerank: /v1/rerank
- completions_legacy: /v1/completions (not protected in MVP; still basic limits)
- misc_low_risk: /v1/models, /v1/health, /v1/files/*, etc.

Policy matrix — Hosted API (defaults)
Notes:
- Values are per API key (account) per region.
- "Sustained" is implemented as rps over 60s smoothing (gateway), but configured as a 1s bucket with refill rate calibrated to ~60s sustained target.
- Quotas are intentionally coarse; enterprise generally uses contract limits and may be “unlimited” in quota service with separate rate limits + budgets.

Table columns
- Sustained RPS: steady-state target
- Burst (req): max burst bucket capacity
- Quota window: billing/quota enforcement window
- Daily quota: requests/day and token/day caps (if applicable)

HOSTED — ENTERPRISE (priority)
| route_group | protected? | sustained_rps | burst_req | quota_window | daily_req_quota | daily_token_quota | overload behavior |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---|
| chat | yes | 50 rps | 300 | monthly (contract) | contract | contract | preserve budget; admit unless extreme; no fallback unless explicitly allowed |
| embeddings | yes | 120 rps | 800 | monthly (contract) | contract | contract | preserve budget; prefer batching; shed only after best-effort fully gated |
| rerank | yes | 80 rps | 500 | monthly (contract) | contract | contract | preserve budget; strict latency SLO; shed best-effort first |
| completions_legacy | no (MVP) | 20 rps | 120 | monthly (contract) | contract | contract | best-effort gating rules NOT applied (yet) |
| misc_low_risk | no | 200 rps | 1000 | n/a | n/a | n/a | never shed (should be tiny) |

HOSTED — PRO (paid, best-effort)
| route_group | protected? | sustained_rps | burst_req | quota_window | daily_req_quota | daily_token_quota | overload behavior |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---|
| chat | yes | 15 rps | 80 | 24h rolling | 1,200,000 | 18B tokens | gated early under pressure; 429 overload_shed expected |
| embeddings | yes | 40 rps | 220 | 24h rolling | 2,000,000 | n/a | gated early; prioritize enterprise + dedicated first |
| rerank | yes | 25 rps | 120 | 24h rolling | 1,500,000 | n/a | gated early; 429 overload_shed expected |
| completions_legacy | no (MVP) | 8 rps | 40 | 24h rolling | 400,000 | 6B tokens | basic rate limiting only |
| misc_low_risk | no | 60 rps | 400 | n/a | n/a | n/a | no shedding |

HOSTED — STANDARD (paid-lite / growth, best-effort)
| route_group | protected? | sustained_rps | burst_req | quota_window | daily_req_quota | daily_token_quota | overload behavior |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---|
| chat | yes | 6 rps | 30 | 24h rolling | 350,000 | 4B tokens | gated aggressively under pressure |
| embeddings | yes | 18 rps | 90 | 24h rolling | 600,000 | n/a | gated aggressively |
| rerank | yes | 10 rps | 50 | 24h rolling | 450,000 | n/a | gated aggressively |
| completions_legacy | no (MVP) | 3 rps | 15 | 24h rolling | 120,000 | 1.5B tokens | basic rate limiting only |
| misc_low_risk | no | 30 rps | 200 | n/a | n/a | n/a | no shedding |

HOSTED — FREE / TRIAL (best-effort)
| route_group | protected? | sustained_rps | burst_req | quota_window | daily_req_quota | daily_token_quota | overload behavior |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---|
| chat | yes | 2 rps | 10 | 24h rolling | 25,000 | 250M tokens | first to be gated; expect frequent 429s during busy periods |
| embeddings | yes | 4 rps | 20 | 24h rolling | 60,000 | n/a | first to be gated |
| rerank | yes | 3 rps | 15 | 24h rolling | 40,000 | n/a | first to be gated |
| completions_legacy | no (MVP) | 1 rps | 5 | 24h rolling | 10,000 | 100M tokens | basic rate limiting only |
| misc_low_risk | no | 10 rps | 80 | n/a | n/a | n/a | no shedding |

Policy matrix — Dedicated tier (defaults)
Notes:
- Dedicated traffic is isolated at the GPU pool level, but gateway protections still prevent self-inflicted overload and protect control plane services.
- Dedicated enterprise customers may request higher bursts; allow only with load-test evidence + per-route SLO review.

DEDICATED — DEFAULT
| route_group | protected? | sustained_rps | burst_req | quota_window | daily_req_quota | daily_token_quota | overload behavior |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---|
| chat | yes | 120 rps | 800 | n/a | n/a | n/a | admission control based on pool queue depth; returns 429 overload_shed before 5xx |
| embeddings | yes | 250 rps | 1500 | n/a | n/a | n/a | prefer batching; backpressure earlier to keep p99 stable |
| rerank | yes | 200 rps | 1200 | n/a | n/a | n/a | keep p95/p99 tight; shed non-critical bursts |
| misc_low_risk | no | 500 rps | 2500 | n/a | n/a | n/a | no shedding |

Shape-based modifiers (proposed; NOT implemented in MVP)
- Motivation: long prompts / large batch sizes correlate strongly with scheduler lag and KV pressure.
- Proposed simple approach (low-cardinality): apply 2–3 “shape buckets” derived from request metadata.
  - chat.prompt_tokens_bucket: <=2k, 2k–8k, >8k
  - embeddings.batch_size_bucket: <=16, 17–64, >64
  - rerank.n_docs_bucket: <=32, 33–128, >128
- Draft multipliers (apply to sustained_rps only):
  - medium bucket: 0.7x
  - large bucket: 0.4x
Open question: can we do this without adding high-cardinality logs/metrics? Jordan/Logan to weigh in.

Overload / admission control mapping (how these numbers are used)
- Gateway tier_rate_limit: always on; prevents obvious abusive spikes.
- Quota: for free/standard/pro. Enterprise typically bypasses quota service (contract) but still uses rate limits.
- Routing admission control:
  - Triggered by capacity signals (scheduler lag, queue depth, GPU saturation) at pool + route_group granularity (where possible).
  - When triggered: gate in order Free → Standard → Pro → (Enterprise last).
  - Enterprise behavior under pressure: maintain defined SLOs; if fully out of budget, return 429 overload_shed rather than slow-drip timeouts.

Exception policy (customer overrides)
- Exceptions are “override records” keyed by account_id + route_group + region (+ optional model_group), reviewed weekly.
- Approval path (current): Solutions Eng (Markus/Simran) + SRE (Rafael/Aisha) + Product (Nikhil) for enterprise.
- Guardrails:
  - Any burst_req > 2x default requires a load test or prior production evidence (graphs) + rollback plan.
  - Any sustained_rps increase > 50% requires confirming dedicated vs hosted pool impact.
  - Overrides expire by default (30 days) unless explicitly extended.

Known enterprise exceptions (tracking list; sanitize before sharing externally)
- ACME AI (prospect / pilot): requested chat burst 2x during eval window; propose enterprise chat burst_req=600 in us-east only (30-day expiry). Owner: Liam O’Rourke.
- Proxima Bank (existing): wants embeddings sustained +50% for nightly batch; prefer moving batch to off-peak window + dedicated add-on rather than raising hosted limits. Owner: Rachel Kim.

Rollout notes
- us-east canary: using above Hosted Enterprise + Pro defaults; observed overload_shed mainly on Free/Standard during bursts; enterprise SLO stable.
- eu-west: early data shows higher tail latency at same thresholds; propose lowering Free/Standard sustained by ~20% until we finish scheduler lag tuning.

Open questions / TODO
- Confirm whether rerank should share a combined budget with embeddings (same pool) or remain separate route_group budget.
- Decide if completions_legacy becomes protected in phase 2 or stays best-effort with basic limits.
- Align quota numbers with pricing/billing constraints (out of scope for this project, but quotas must not conflict with plan entitlements).
- Add “retry guidance” snippet to Support macro: which 429 reason codes are safe to retry and recommended backoff.

Changelog (short)
- 2026-01-22: Adjusted Hosted Pro chat sustained_rps 12→15 based on post-canary headroom; clarified exception expiry default.
- 2026-01-08: Added Dedicated defaults and overload behavior notes.
- 2025-12-10: Initial matrix draft created from discovery data + SRE recommendations.
